newsitem.title: GEORGIA: Georgian leader drops security minister.
newsitem.headline: Georgian leader drops security minister.

text.p: Georgian President Eduard Shevardnadze accepted the resignation of his embattled security minister on Saturday, the presidential press service said.
The president did not immediately name a successor to Shota Kviraya. The press service said Shevardnadze had removed the minister at his own request.
Last month, parliament abandoned an attempt to impeach Kviraya and asked Shevardnadze to take a final decision on his fate.

A group of parliamentary members have alleged Kviraya executed six suspected looters during a 1993 civil war, authorised the bugging of several journalists' telephones and worked for Russian intelligence services.
Kviraya has denied the charges. It was not immediately clear why he decided to submit his resignation.
